adr_content.title: ADR-0223 — oya git as drop-in surface for git; policy verbs stay explicit; no implicit state derivation
adr_content.status: Proposed (promotes to Accepted when PR-159A lands)
context: PR-159 directive 2026-05-18: `oya vcs` → `oya git`. Drop-in for git semantics + ledger/policy layer.

Intermediate synthesis proposed: implicit state machine driven by git verbs (add = claim; commit = work; push = done). And: auto-PR creation on push. And: cross-agent conflict-radar via shared file-claim ledger.
Doubt-driven cross-examination 2026-05-18 surfaced specific fail modes in those over-extensions; the core (drop-in + ledger) survives, the over-extensions do not.

decision.core: `oya git <verb>` is a drop-in surface for raw git: bit-perfect stdout, identical exit code, git's stderr + optional `oya:` prefixed informational lines, per-verb ledger emission to .oya/ledger/audit-chain.jsonl. Hyrum's Law lock: drop-in semantics may NEVER drift from git's observable behavior; ledger layer can only ADD non-observable behavior.
decision.policy_verbs_stay_explicit: `oya claim <work-id>` and `oya submit` remain SEPARATE explicit verbs, NOT derived from git actions. Agent runs these when intent demands; git verbs do not auto-trigger policy state transitions.
decision.no_auto_pr_on_push: `oya git push` does ONLY git push. PR creation lives in the explicit `oya submit` verb (which already exists: verify + push + open/extend PR with title + body + draft state).
decision.no_conflict_radar_in_v1: Worktree isolation per ADR-0116 plus merge-queue serialization per ADR-0111 already address parallel-agent conflicts. Conflict-radar is DEFERRED until measured data shows the existing architecture is insufficient.
decision.no_implicit_state_machine: Claim/work/done state transitions are NOT inferred from git verbs. Reason: claim end-timing is ambiguous (per-push? per-branch? per-merged-cycle?). Re-push after CI-red would either create N claims or amend opaquely. Rebase/amend break ledger SHA references. Multi-branch work for one logical unit is opaque. No clean mapping exists.

alternatives_considered.option: Implicit state machine (`oya git add` auto-claims; `oya git push` marks done)
rejected_because: Claim END timing is ambiguous across legitimate workflows (CI-fix loops, rebase, multi-branch)
`git rebase` rewrites history; ledger entries reference dangling SHAs
Conflates two cadences: git events (per-commit) vs claim lifecycle (per-logical-unit-of-work)
Surfaces wrong half the time → agent fights the state machine
Drop-in latency: PR creation adds 500ms-3s; breaks drop-in feel
Heuristic title/body wrong ~50% of cases (commit subject 'fix' tells reviewers nothing)
`gh auth` is fragile dependency; failure mode is silent (push succeeds, PR doesn't open)
Removes safeguard for 'I pushed to test, not ready' workflow
PR template integration is non-trivial; empty template is reviewer noise
Worktree isolation (ADR-0116 layer-0) already prevents local conflicts
Merge queue (ADR-0111 projected-merge-state) already serializes upstream conflicts
Marginal benefit; large infra cost (atomic JSONL append, TTL handling, stale-claim GC)
Premature without measured data showing parallel-conflict pain

alternatives_considered.option: Multi-VCS abstraction (`oya vcs` keeping the layer-agnostic name; future jj/sapling support)
rejected_because: Never used the abstraction; we're git-only and have been forever
Locks us to nothing more than git already does (jj/sapling adoption is theoretical)
Honesty: drop-in for git is the directive; name should reflect implementation

alternatives_considered.option: Status quo (`oya vcs <verb>` + `oya submit` + raw `git` for everything else)
rejected_because: PR-143 step 10 live-validated the gap: had to fall back to raw `git commit`, `git stash`, `git checkout HEAD --` because oya surface didn't have the verbs
Cross-agent inconsistency (Claude vs Codex vs Gemini use different fallback paths)
No ledger substrate → no replay-driven debugging → no throughput telemetry

consequences_positive: Anyone with git knowledge productive immediately — zero new commands to learn for the verb surface
Drop-in invariant locks behavior: no accidental semantic drift; Hyrum's Law works FOR us
Ledger substrate enables: audit chain at action layer, replay-driven debugging, throughput telemetry
Smaller PR-159B scope (~1500 LOC vs ~2500 LOC); ships faster
Policy verbs remain explicit → agent intent stays legible → reviewers understand 'why this push'
No `gh auth` brittleness in the verb surface (auto-PR friction confined to `oya submit`)

consequences_negative_and_mitigations.consequence: Two surfaces (git verbs + policy verbs) instead of one unified surface
consequences_negative_and_mitigations.mitigation: Documentation makes the line clear: `oya git <verb>` = git, `oya claim`/`oya submit` = policy. Hooks suggest the right verb based on user intent (PR-160 scope).

consequences_negative_and_mitigations.consequence: Drop-in latency: shell-out to git adds ~30-100ms
consequences_negative_and_mitigations.mitigation: Acceptable for human use. Measure agent throughput impact (task #39 baseline). v2 libgit2-native if data warrants.

consequences_negative_and_mitigations.consequence: Hyrum's Law on stderr — informational `oya:` lines may be parsed by some script
consequences_negative_and_mitigations.mitigation: Document the `oya:` prefix as informational + stable; provide `oya git --quiet` to suppress; ledger-via-side-channel (.oya/ledger/) for anything machine-readable.

consequences_negative_and_mitigations.consequence: `oya git` name contains `git` substring → forbidden_primitives validator may trip
consequences_negative_and_mitigations.mitigation: Coordinate with F-FORBIDDEN-PRIMITIVES-CI-GUARD lane build. Word-boundary regex, not substring.

consequences_negative_and_mitigations.consequence: Top-level oya surface gets crowded (existing `oya verify`, `oya gate`, etc.)
consequences_negative_and_mitigations.mitigation: Out of scope for this ADR. Future migration could move git-adjacent ops under `oya git` namespace (e.g., `oya git verify`); separate ADR if pursued.

consequences_negative_and_mitigations.consequence: PR-159A rename touches ~50+ files; CI scripts grepping `oya vcs` break silently
consequences_negative_and_mitigations.mitigation: Add deprecation-window CI lane that warns on `oya vcs <verb>` invocations. Ship rename + deprecation lane together.

out_of_scope_for_this_ADR: Implicit claim derivation from git verbs (CUT)
Auto-PR on push (CUT — lives in `oya submit`)
Migration of `oya verify` / `oya gate` etc. under `oya git` namespace (SEPARATE ADR if pursued)
references: ADR-0116 — retired external agent coordination tooling (grit/rtk/icm/vox)
ADR-0111 — merge queue projected merge state
ADR-0132 — product suite and bundle dissolution + governance glossary

doubt_driven_findings_summary.core_concept_verified: `oya git` as drop-in surface for git with ledger emission per verb — SURVIVES doubt-driven cross-examination

over_extensions_cut.item: Implicit state machine from git verbs
over_extensions_cut.reason: Claim end-timing ambiguity; rebase/amend break SHA references; cadence mismatch
Heuristic brittleness; drop-in violation; removes 'push to test' safeguard; gh auth fragility
Worktree isolation + merge queue already handle parallel-agent conflicts; premature without data

open_risks_with_mitigations: Stderr Hyrum's Law (oya: prefix documented + --quiet flag)
PR-159A rename CI breakage (deprecation-window warn lane)

PR_159A.before: Rename oya vcs → oya git across surfaces
PR_159A.after: Same scope + deprecation-window CI lane that warns on `oya vcs <verb>` invocations
PR_159A.size: thin — ~50 file textual rename + 1 new CI lane

PR_159B.before: Verb surface + auto-PR + implicit state machine + conflict-radar (~2500 LOC)
PR_159B.after: Verb surface + ledger emission ONLY (~1500 LOC)

new_task_39.scope: Baseline throughput measurement BEFORE PR-159B engineering
new_task_39.reason: Don't optimize blind. If CI runtime dominates (likely), agent-side wrapper won't move the throughput needle until CI parallelism/caching is addressed.

PR_160.before: Hook integration suggesting `oya vcs <verb>` on `git <verb>` detection
PR_160.after: Hook integration suggesting `oya git <verb>` on `git <verb>` detection PLUS oya-git-event hooks (post-verb side channel) for ledger consumption
PR_160.size: moderate — extends PR-158 hook payload + adds event hook category

verdict: Concept core is sound; revised scope captured; ADR-0223 ready for promotion when PR-159A opens.
